Origami

One sheet of paper is the whole film: it fanfolds into a stack of printed dashboards, opens into the Acme mark, peeks open to show the anomaly on its inner face, and refolds into an envelope. Crisp creases, faceted shading, teal ink — coral lives only inside the folds.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Fold panel — a plane that rotates on its hinge edge with backface hidden; the unit of every transition
  • Crease line — dashed hairline that appears 4 frames before a fold — the visual count-in
  • Facet shade — panel fill darkens with its fold angle, giving depth without 3D
  • Inner face — the coral back side of a fold; the only place the anomaly colour appears
  • Blintz flaps — four triangles that open around the centre square for the logo reveal
  • Dog-ear button — paper tag with a folded corner used for “Roll back” and “Start free”

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Accordion unfold — each panel rotates 180→0°, power3.inOut 0.45 s, staggered by 0.25 s (an eighth note at 120 BPM)
  • Crease pre-flash — 4-frame dashed line + 2° pre-bend before every fold, so the eye knows where the paper will break before the beat
  • Peek fold — rotateY 0 → 30°, expo.out 0.3 s, hold 1 s (2 beats), then complete to 180° on the next downbeat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Folding is a perfect metaphor for “hidden until it matters”: everything looks calm on the outside and the problem is literally on the inside of the fold. Paper feels precise and honest. Risk: diagonal CSS-3D folds are fiddly — pre-plan every hinge edge and keep text on panels that face camera.

Adapt to your product: Print your product's key screen onto the sheet and pick the one thing it surfaces as the inner face; any list-type UI (orders, tickets, builds) folds naturally into a tri-fold or accordion.

References: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2012/10/17/pfold-paper-like-unfolding-effect/ (paper-like unfolding in CSS) · https://github.com/joumorisu/CSS-Origami (CSS origami experiments)
